corporate-tax-return.title: Corporate Tax Return
corporate-tax-return.content:
At Bajwa CPA Professional Corporation, we offer a wide variety of services for our corporate clients. By keeping current on the tax laws and legislation in Canada, we give incorporated businesses in Brampton, Mississauga and across the Greater Toronto Area the expertise needed to file their corporate tax returns correctly and on time. We work with corporate clients from many different sectors, so we deliver tax solutions and advice in an efficient, practical way.

When you work with us, your file is handled by a licensed CPA, you get a fixed quote before work begins, and you have support all year, not just at year end. If you have questions about tax brackets, tax rates, tax credits or deadlines, one of our experts can answer them at any time.

Why Your Corporate Tax Return Needs a CPA

Every corporation resident in Canada must file a T2 Corporation Income Tax Return each year, even if it earned no income or owes no tax. The return is due within six months of your fiscal year end, but any balance owing is usually due much earlier. Missing these dates leads to CRA penalties and interest that add up quickly.

A T2 return is more than a form. It includes several schedules, the Ontario corporate tax calculation, GIFI financial data and, in many cases, year-end adjusting entries. Small errors can mean a missed small business deduction, a lost tax credit or a CRA review. Our team prepares each return carefully so your corporation pays only what it owes.

Worried about T2 deadlines or CRA penalties? Let a CPA take it off your plate.

Call 416-907-0568Get My Fixed Quote

The Corporate Tax Services We Offer

Corporate Tax Returns (T2) Preparation & Filing

We prepare corporate tax returns, tax return schedules, tax instalments, proposed year-end adjusting entries and filings with CRA. Each return is reviewed by a CPA before it is filed.

T4 & T5 Slips

We prepare and file T4 slips (employment income) and T5 slips (dividends) for income you receive from your corporation as an employee or shareholder. We can also help you decide on the right mix of salary and dividends.

HST Returns

We prepare and file HST returns for corporations, whether you file monthly, quarterly or annually. Learn more about HST support for smaller operations on our business tax return page.

Payroll Services

We prepare payroll for employees working in your corporation and handle source deduction remittances with CRA.

Compilation Services

We prepare Notice to Reader (compilation) financial statements by compiling your corporation’s financial information. See our financial statement preparation services for details.

Bookkeeping, General Ledgers & Financial Statement Preparation

We provide full-cycle bookkeeping for our clients on a monthly, quarterly or annual basis. Clean books make your year-end T2 faster, cheaper and more accurate. Explore our bookkeeping services in Brampton and Mississauga.

Corporate Tax Planning

Our experienced staff develop tax planning and tax-minimization strategies to improve your after-tax position. We look after your corporate tax planning and filing needs, make sure you meet every filing deadline, help reduce CRA penalties and interest, and support your corporation’s financial goals. For a deeper look, visit our tax planning services.

One team for your T2, HST, payroll and bookkeeping. Find out what your corporation could save.

Book a Free ConsultationCall 416-907-0568

Our Corporate Tax Return Process

  1. Free consultation. We learn about your corporation, its year end, its industry and any open CRA matters.
  2. Fixed quote. You receive a clear price before any work begins, so there are no surprises.
  3. Document collection. We send a simple checklist. Our tax checklists page shows what most corporations need.
  4. Bookkeeping review and adjustments. We review your books, propose year-end adjusting entries and prepare your financial statements.
  5. T2 preparation and CPA review. We prepare the return and schedules, and a CPA reviews them for accuracy and tax savings.
  6. Filing and follow-up. We file with CRA, confirm instalments for the next year and stay available for any CRA questions.

Corporations We Work With

Our business has been built mainly on referrals from existing clients. We file corporate returns for consultants, doctors, dentists, chiropractors, pharmacists, travel agencies, startups, construction companies, retail stores, automotive businesses, food and entertainment businesses, real estate brokerages, financial services firms and franchises.

We also work with professional corporations. If you are a regulated professional thinking about incorporating, our incorporation and business registration services can help you set up correctly from day one.

Incorporated professional or growing business? Talk to a Brampton CPA who knows your industry.

Contact Us TodayCall 416-907-0568

Serving Corporations Across the GTA and Ontario

Our office is at 2 County Court Blvd, Suite 400, in Brampton, a short drive from Mississauga, Caledon, Bolton, Georgetown and Milton. We also serve corporations in Toronto, Etobicoke, Vaughan, Oakville and across Ontario. Most of our work can be completed securely online, so you can work with a Brampton and Mississauga corporate tax accountant wherever your business is located in Ontario.

Personalized for Your Business

At Bajwa CPA, we take the time to learn about and understand each client’s business to make sure we truly meet their needs and provide outstanding professional service. Our goal is to deliver our services in an easy-to-understand manner that is both timely and reliable. You can trust us with your corporate tax return because our team has the expertise to complete it thoroughly and professionally.

Many of our corporate clients also ask us to file their personal tax returns, so salary, dividends and personal deductions are planned together. Owners with rental or investment property can also use our real estate tax return services.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is my corporate tax return due?

A T2 return is due within six months of your corporation’s fiscal year end. Any tax owing is generally due two or three months after year end, depending on your corporation’s situation. We track these dates for you.

Does my corporation need to file if it had no income?

Yes. Every resident corporation must file a T2 return each year, even if it was inactive or had no income.

How much does a corporate tax return cost?

The fee depends on the size of your corporation and the condition of your books. We give you a fixed quote after a free consultation, before any work begins.

Can you file late or past-due corporate returns?

Yes. We help corporations catch up on unfiled T2 returns and work to reduce penalties and interest with CRA where possible.

Do I have to visit your Brampton office?

No. You are welcome to meet us in Brampton, but most clients in Mississauga, Toronto and across Ontario share documents securely online.

Get Started on Your Corporate Tax Return

Looking for a reliable corporate tax accountant in Brampton or Mississauga? Call 416-907-0568 or contact us today to book a free consultation and get a fixed quote for your T2 return.

business-tax-return.title: Business Tax Return
business-tax-return.content:
We help you file your business tax returns for unincorporated businesses. If you are a sole proprietor, a partnership or a self-employed professional running a small business in Brampton, Mississauga or anywhere in the Greater Toronto Area, we provide affordable, professional monthly bookkeeping support, accounting services, HST return preparation and tax filing services. We can also guide you through registering or incorporating your business.

Your return is prepared and reviewed by a licensed CPA. You get a fixed quote up front and support all year, so questions about expenses, HST or CRA letters never have to wait until tax season.

Why Self-Employed Business Owners Choose a CPA

When you run an unincorporated business, your business income is reported on your personal T1 return using Form T2125. That means business decisions directly affect your personal tax bill. Claiming the wrong expenses, mixing personal and business costs or missing HST deadlines can lead to reassessments, penalties and interest.

Self-employed individuals have until June 15 to file, but any balance owing is still due on April 30. Many business owners also need to make quarterly instalments. We keep track of these dates and help you plan ahead, so tax time is predictable instead of stressful.

Not sure which expenses you can claim? A CPA will find every deduction you are owed.

Call 416-907-0568Get My Fixed Quote

The Business Tax Services We Offer

Statement of Business or Professional Activities (T2125)

The Statement of Business or Professional Activities is the form self-employed individuals use to report business income and expenses. We prepare it carefully, claiming every eligible expense, including home office, vehicle, phone, supplies and capital cost allowance on equipment.

HST Returns Preparation and Filing

We help you prepare and file your HST return before the due date to avoid penalties and interest. In general, you must register for HST once your taxable revenue goes over $30,000 in four consecutive calendar quarters. We can register you, choose the right filing frequency and explain whether the Quick Method could save you money.

Payroll Services for Your Employees

Every business has its own payroll needs. We take the time to understand your business and manage your payroll, tax forms, source deduction remittances, T4 slips and reports.

Bookkeeping, General Ledgers & Financial Statement Preparation

Let us handle your bookkeeping and financial statements so you can focus on running your business. Organised monthly books make your year-end return faster and more accurate. See our monthly bookkeeping packages and financial statement services.

Business Tax Planning

We help you prepare for the upcoming tax year so your business operates at its best. This includes instalment planning, timing of large purchases, RRSP contributions and deciding when it makes sense to incorporate. Learn more on our tax planning page.

Business Registration and Incorporation

Starting out, or ready to grow? We can register your sole proprietorship or partnership in Ontario, or help you move to a corporation when the tax savings justify it. Visit our incorporation and business registration page for details.

T2125, HST, payroll and bookkeeping, all handled by one local team.

Book a Free ConsultationCall 416-907-0568

Who We Help

We work with self-employed people and small businesses across many industries, including:

  • Consultants and independent contractors
  • Real estate agents and brokerages
  • Construction and trades
  • Retail businesses
  • Travel agencies
  • Food and entertainment businesses
  • Automotive businesses
  • Financial services professionals
  • Franchise owners
  • Startups and new small businesses

If you earn rental income alongside your business, our real estate tax return services can cover your property reporting in the same file.

Should You Stay a Sole Proprietor or Incorporate?

This is one of the most common questions we get from business owners in Brampton and Mississauga. A sole proprietorship is simple and inexpensive to run. A corporation can offer lower tax rates on profits you leave in the business, along with limited liability, but it comes with extra filing and accounting costs.

We review your income, expenses and goals and show you the numbers side by side. If incorporating makes sense, we can handle the setup and later prepare your corporate tax return.

Should you incorporate this year? Get a side-by-side tax comparison from our CPA.

Ask a CPACall 416-907-0568

Our Simple Process

  1. Free consultation to understand your business and any open CRA matters.
  2. Fixed quote before we begin, so you know the cost up front.
  3. Document checklist so you know exactly what to send. See our tax checklists.
  4. Preparation and CPA review of your T2125, T1 and HST returns.
  5. E-filing with CRA and a clear summary of what you owe or will receive.
  6. Year-round support for CRA letters, instalments and planning.

Serving Small Businesses Across the GTA and Ontario

Our office is in Brampton at 2 County Court Blvd, Suite 400, close to Mississauga, Caledon, Bolton, Georgetown and Milton. We also serve self-employed clients in Toronto, Etobicoke, Vaughan, Oakville and across Ontario, with secure online document sharing for clients who prefer not to visit in person.

Tailored to Your Small Business

At Bajwa CPA, we take the time to learn about and understand each client’s business to make sure we truly meet their needs and provide outstanding professional service. Our goal is to deliver our services in an easy-to-understand manner that is both timely and reliable. Because your business income flows onto your personal tax return, we look at the whole picture, not just one form.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the deadline for a self-employed tax return?

Self-employed individuals must file by June 15. Any balance owing is due by April 30, and interest starts after that date.

What business expenses can I claim?

Common expenses include advertising, supplies, rent, a portion of home office costs, vehicle expenses, phone and internet, professional fees and capital cost allowance on equipment. We confirm what applies to your business.

Do I need to register for HST?

Generally, yes, once your taxable revenue goes over $30,000 in four consecutive calendar quarters. Some businesses register earlier by choice to claim input tax credits.

Can you help if I have not filed for a few years?

Yes. We can prepare and file past-due returns and help you deal with CRA to reduce penalties and interest where possible.

How much does a business tax return cost?

It depends on your number of transactions and how organised your records are. You get a fixed quote after a free consultation.

Book Your Consultation

Need a self-employed tax accountant in Brampton or Mississauga? Call 416-907-0568 or contact us today to book a consultation and get a fixed quote for your business tax return.

bookkeeping.title: Bookkeeping
bookkeeping.content:
Keeping your company’s books up to date and accurate is critical to measuring growth, planning for the future and filing accurate year-end tax returns. Bajwa CPA helps businesses in Brampton, Mississauga and across the Greater Toronto Area run smoothly with efficient, effective accounting and bookkeeping services based on sound accounting principles.

Whether you are a corporation, a sole proprietor or an unincorporated business, we look after all your accounting and bookkeeping needs with personalized, one-on-one service. Our QuickBooks ProAdvisor certified team are experts in bookkeeping and accounting principles. We keep your books timely and accurate so you can see your true financial position, meet your goals and manage your business with confidence.

Every bookkeeping file is overseen by a licensed CPA, priced at a fixed monthly rate and supported all year.

Why Accurate Bookkeeping Matters

Good books do more than keep CRA happy. They show you which products or clients are profitable, where cash is going and whether you can afford to hire or expand. When your records are up to date, your year-end corporate tax return or business tax return is faster, cheaper and far less stressful.

Poor or late bookkeeping often leads to missed expenses, HST errors, cash flow surprises and expensive clean-up work at year end. Regular monthly bookkeeping prevents these problems before they start.

Behind on your books? We catch up, clean up and keep you current every month.

Call 416-907-0568Get a Free Consultation

Our Accounting and Bookkeeping Services

Our firm provides a full range of cost-effective accounting and bookkeeping services, including:

Bookkeeping (Monthly, Quarterly & Annual)

We record your sales, expenses and payments on a schedule that fits your business, whether that is weekly, monthly, quarterly or once a year.

General Ledger & Financial Statement Preparation

We maintain your general ledger and prepare clear financial statements so you always know where your business stands.

Accounting System Setup for New Businesses

Starting a business? We set up QuickBooks Online, Xero, Wave or FreshBooks correctly from day one, with a chart of accounts that fits your industry. If you are still registering, see our incorporation and business registration services.

Compilation of Financial Statements (NTR)

As your business grows and new opportunities arise, banks and lenders may ask to see your financial position. We can efficiently prepare your Notice to Reader financial statements so you can obtain financing.

Fixed monthly pricing, no long-term contract. See which package fits your business.

Find My PackageCall 416-907-0568

  4. Ongoing bookkeeping. We record, reconcile and review your books on your chosen schedule.

  6. Year-end ready. Your books are ready for your tax return and year-round tax planning.

Ready for books you can trust at tax time? Start with a free call.

Contact Us TodayCall 416-907-0568

Industries We Keep Books For

We provide bookkeeping for consultants, doctors, dentists, chiropractors, travel agencies, startups, construction companies, retail stores, automotive businesses, food and entertainment businesses, real estate brokerages, financial services firms and franchises. Landlords with several properties can pair bookkeeping with our real estate tax return services.

Bookkeeping Across the GTA and Ontario

Our team works from our Brampton office at 2 County Court Blvd, Suite 400, serving businesses in Brampton, Mississauga, Caledon, Bolton, Georgetown, Milton, Toronto, Etobicoke, Vaughan and Oakville. Because we work in the cloud, we provide online bookkeeping to businesses anywhere in Ontario.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between cash and accrual bookkeeping?

Cash basis records income and expenses when money is received or paid. Accrual basis records them when they are earned or incurred, which gives a more accurate picture for growing businesses and corporations.

Which accounting software do you work with?

We work with QuickBooks Online, Xero, Wave and FreshBooks, and can set up and train you on any of them.

Can you catch up on months or years of missed bookkeeping?

Yes. We regularly clean up and catch up on past records so you can file overdue tax and HST returns.

Is there a long-term contract?

No. Our packages run month to month. Prepaying annually lowers the monthly price.

Do you file my HST as part of bookkeeping?

personal-tax-return.content:
Our tax firm is committed to providing high-quality personal tax return preparation (T1 General) for individuals and families in Brampton, Mississauga and across the Greater Toronto Area. We are highly experienced in handling a wide variety of personal tax returns. Canadian tax rules are always changing, and it takes skilled professionals to stay current. We provide fast, accurate service to help you keep more of your income.

If you earn employment, interest, rental, employment insurance or self-employment income, we can help you file your tax return accurately and on time. Your return is prepared and reviewed by a licensed CPA, you get a fixed quote before we start, and we are here all year if CRA sends a letter.

Why Use a CPA for Your Personal Taxes?

It may seem simple enough to do your taxes on your own, but it is not worth risking a mistake that could cost you. Let us help with your return so you can avoid filing adjustment returns, paying penalties or missing out on a refund.

Many people miss deductions and credits they are entitled to, such as medical expenses, childcare costs, moving expenses, tuition, donations, RRSP and FHSA deductions, and pension income splitting. Others get reassessed because a slip was missed or rental and business expenses were claimed incorrectly. Our team reviews your full situation to make sure every eligible claim is made and every slip is reported.

We are also very proficient in personal and business tax planning, using tax-minimization strategies that lower what you pay year after year. See our tax planning services to learn more.

Don’t leave money with CRA. Let a CPA find every credit and deduction you qualify for.

Call 416-907-0568Book My Appointment

Examples of Our Personal Tax Return Services

Income From Employment (T4 Slips)

We report your employment income correctly and claim related credits and deductions.

Investment Income

Interest, dividends and capital gains from T3, T5 and T5008 slips, including capital losses carried forward.

Limited Partnerships

Reporting of partnership income and losses from T5013 slips.

Rental Income

Reporting rental income and expenses for houses, condos and basement units. For investors and multiple properties, see our real estate tax return services.

Professional Income

Income for self-employed professionals such as consultants, doctors, dentists and other practitioners.

Commission Income

Returns for commissioned salespeople, real estate agents and others who earn commission, including eligible expenses.

Business Income / Unincorporated Businesses

If you are self-employed, your business income is reported on Form T2125 with your T1 return. Learn more on our business tax return page.

EI, Old Age Security & Social Security Benefit Income

Reporting of EI, CPP, OAS and foreign social security or pension benefits.

Adjustments and Amendments to T1 Tax Returns

Missed a slip or a deduction in a past year? We file T1 adjustment requests to correct prior returns.

Filing Objections and Appeals With CRA

If you disagree with a CRA reassessment, we can prepare and file a notice of objection on your behalf.

Allowable Employee Expenses

Claims for eligible employment expenses supported by a signed T2200 or T2200S from your employer.

Departure Tax Returns

Leaving Canada? We prepare your final return as a resident, including any departure tax on deemed dispositions. After you leave, our non-resident tax return services can help you stay compliant.

New Immigrant Tax Returns

Newcomers to Canada have special rules for their first return, including reporting world income only from the date they arrived. Filing on time also helps you start receiving benefits such as the GST/HST credit and Canada Child Benefit.

Deceased Tax Returns

We prepare the final T1 return for a person who has passed away and guide the executor on next steps. Estates may also need a T3 return; see our trust and estate tax return services.

Rental income, newcomer, late filing or a CRA letter? We handle the tricky returns too.

Get My Fixed QuoteCall 416-907-0568

Our Personal Tax Filing Process

  1. Book an appointment in person at our Brampton office or online.
  2. Get a fixed quote based on your situation before any work starts.
  3. Send your documents using our tax checklists as a guide.
  4. Preparation and CPA review to catch errors and find every credit.
  5. E-filing with CRA and a clear summary of your refund or balance owing.
  6. Year-round support for CRA letters, reviews and next year’s planning.

Key Personal Tax Deadlines

For most people, the personal tax filing deadline is April 30, and any balance owing is due on the same day. Self-employed individuals and their spouses have until June 15 to file, but any balance owing is still due by April 30. Filing late can lead to penalties and can delay benefits and credits. Visit our tax filing deadlines page for the full calendar.

April 30 comes fast. Book early and file stress-free.

Book Before the DeadlineCall 416-907-0568

Personal Tax Services Across the GTA and Ontario

Our office is at 2 County Court Blvd, Suite 400, in Brampton. We file personal tax returns for individuals and families in Brampton, Mississauga, Caledon, Bolton, Georgetown, Milton, Toronto, Etobicoke, Vaughan, Oakville and throughout Ontario. You can meet us in person or share your documents securely online.

If you also own a corporation, we can prepare your corporate tax return at the same time, so your salary, dividends and personal deductions are planned together.

Trust in the Professionals at Bajwa CPA

At Bajwa CPA, we take the time to learn about and understand each client’s personal situation to make sure we truly meet their needs and provide outstanding professional service. Our goal is to deliver our services in an easy-to-understand manner that is both timely and reliable.

Frequently Asked Questions

What documents do I need for my personal tax return?

Your T-slips (T4, T5, T3, T4A and others), receipts for deductions such as RRSP, childcare, medical and donations, and records of rental or business income and expenses. Our tax checklist lists everything.

Can you file tax returns for previous years?

Yes. We can file late returns for past years and request adjustments to returns you have already filed.

I am new to Canada. Do I need to file?

In most cases, yes. Filing your first return helps you get benefits and credits, and we make sure your world income is reported correctly for the part of the year before you arrived.

How much does a personal tax return cost?

It depends on your income sources and how complex your return is. We give you a fixed quote before we begin.

What if CRA reviews or reassesses my return?

We help you respond to CRA review letters and, if needed, file an objection on your behalf.

Book Your Personal Tax Appointment

Looking for a personal tax accountant in Brampton or Mississauga? Call 416-907-0568 or contact us today to book an appointment and get your return filed accurately and on time.

non-resident-tax-returns.title: Non-Resident Tax Return
non-resident-tax-returns.content:
As a non-resident of Canada, you are still subject to Canadian income tax. Most Canadian-source income paid or credited to you during the year can be taxed, unless all or part of it is exempt under a tax treaty. At Bajwa CPA Professional Corporation, we file your tax returns and elections effectively and on time, so you do not pay unnecessary additional tax.

From our office in Brampton, we help non-residents who own property, earn rental or pension income, or are selling real estate in Brampton, Mississauga, the Greater Toronto Area and across Ontario. Your file is handled by a licensed CPA, priced with a fixed quote, and supported all year.

Why Non-Residents Need Specialist Help

Non-resident tax rules are different from the rules for Canadian residents. Canadian payers, such as tenants, property managers and pension plans, are often required to withhold tax from payments to non-residents. For example, rent paid to a non-resident is generally subject to 25% withholding on the gross amount unless the right forms are filed.

Missing an election, a deadline or a clearance certificate can mean paying far more tax than you owe, or having a large amount held back from a property sale. The right filings can often reduce withholding and recover tax that was withheld.

Renting out or selling property in Canada while living abroad? Don’t pay more tax than you owe.

Call 416-907-0568Get My Fixed Quote

Our Tax Services for Non-Residents of Canada

Section 116 Return and Clearance Certificates (T2062 / T2062A)

When a non-resident of Canada sells certain Canadian property, such as real estate, CRA must be notified. We help you prepare and submit the Section 116 notification and apply for a clearance certificate, so the buyer does not have to withhold a large portion of the sale price.

NR4 Slips

We prepare NR4 statements of amounts paid or credited to non-residents of Canada.

NR6 Undertaking

An NR6 is an undertaking to file a Section 216 income tax return by a non-resident receiving rent from Canadian rental property. Once approved, withholding can be based on net rental income instead of gross rent.

Section 216 Return

Non-residents use this return to report rental income from Canadian rental property. Filing it can lead to a refund of excess tax withheld.

Section 217 Return

For non-residents receiving Old Age Security, RRSP, RRIF, pension income and certain other benefits. This election can reduce the tax withheld on these payments.

NR7 Refund Applications

We prepare NR7 applications for a refund of Part XIII tax that was withheld.

NR73 and Residency Analysis

Leaving Canada? We review your residency status, including the NR73 Determination of Residency Status form, and give you an expert review of your ties to Canada.

Section 216, 217 or 116? We’ll tell you exactly which filings you need.

Book a ConsultationCall 416-907-0568

Leaving Canada? Plan Before You Go

Becoming a non-resident has important tax consequences. In your year of departure, you file a final return as a resident, which may include departure tax on certain property. Our personal tax return services cover departure returns. After you leave, we help you stay compliant on any Canadian income you continue to earn.

Planning before you move can make a big difference. Our tax planning services include non-resident tax planning, so you understand the tax impact of keeping or selling property in Canada.

Non-Residents With Canadian Property

Many of our non-resident clients own homes or rental units in Brampton, Mississauga and the GTA. We prepare the rental reporting your property needs and explain the withholding your tenant or property manager must make. For investors with several properties, see our real estate tax return services.

If a non-resident is a beneficiary or executor of a Canadian estate, our trust and estate tax return services can help with the estate’s filings.

Our Process

  1. Consultation. We review your residency, Canadian income and any property you own or plan to sell.
  2. Fixed quote. You know the full cost before any work begins.
  3. Filing plan. We tell you which forms, elections and deadlines apply to you.
  4. Preparation and CPA review. We prepare each return and form, and a CPA reviews it.
  5. Filing and CRA follow-up. We file with CRA and handle any follow-up questions.
  6. Ongoing support. We keep you on track each year for as long as you have Canadian income.

Living outside Canada but earning income here? Get a CPA on your side.

Contact Us TodayCall 416-907-0568

Key Deadlines for Non-Residents

Non-resident filings have their own deadlines, and they are different from the regular April 30 date most Canadians know. Section 216 returns generally have a longer filing window, but the deadline is shorter if you filed an NR6, because you agreed to file on time in exchange for lower withholding. NR4 slips must be issued by the payer within set dates after year end, and a Section 116 notice must be sent to CRA soon after a property sale.

Missing these dates can lead to the loss of lower withholding, penalties or a large amount of the sale price being held back. We track the deadlines that apply to you and file on time, so your Canadian income is handled correctly while you live abroad.

Serving Non-Residents With Ties to the GTA and Ontario

Our office is at 2 County Court Blvd, Suite 400, in Brampton. We serve non-residents with property or income in Brampton, Mississauga, Toronto, Caledon, Vaughan, Oakville, Milton and across Ontario.

At Bajwa CPA, we take the time to learn about and understand each client’s situation to make sure we truly meet their needs and provide outstanding professional service. Our goal is to deliver our services in an easy-to-understand manner that is both timely and reliable.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do non-residents have to pay tax in Canada?

Yes, on most Canadian-source income, such as rent, pensions and gains on Canadian real estate. Tax treaties may reduce or remove the tax on some income.

How much tax is withheld on rent paid to a non-resident?

Generally 25% of the gross rent, unless an NR6 is filed and approved, in which case withholding can be based on net rental income.

What happens if I sell Canadian property as a non-resident?

You generally need to notify CRA under Section 116 and obtain a clearance certificate. Without it, the buyer may have to withhold a large part of the purchase price.

Can I get back tax that was withheld?

Often, yes. Filing a Section 216 or 217 return, or an NR7 application, can result in a refund of excess tax withheld.

How do I know if I am a non-resident?

Residency depends on your ties to Canada, such as a home, spouse or dependants. We review your situation and can help with an NR73 if needed.

Get Help With Your Non-Resident Tax Return

Need a non-resident tax accountant in Brampton or Mississauga? Call 416-907-0568 or contact us today to book a consultation and discuss your Canadian tax needs.

Whether you invest in real estate to earn rental income or buy and sell property for profit, Bajwa CPA Professional Corporation can file your real estate tax returns efficiently and help you save with tax minimization strategies. Real estate can be owned in two ways: individually or through a corporation. We are well experienced in both situations.

We work with landlords, investors and property owners in Brampton, Mississauga and across the Greater Toronto Area, one of Canada’s most active property markets. Every return is prepared and reviewed by a licensed CPA, you get a fixed quote before work begins, and we support you all year.

Why Real Estate Investors Need a CPA

There are many situations and ever-changing tax laws when it comes to real estate investing. The real estate industry is under constant scrutiny by CRA, so to save tax on real estate income it is very important to work with experienced tax professionals.

Common mistakes include claiming capital expenses as repairs, missing allowable expenses, reporting a sale the wrong way or forgetting to report a sale at all. These errors can lead to reassessments, penalties and interest. A CPA helps you claim everything you are entitled to while staying compliant.

Own a rental or sold a property this year? Make sure CRA sees it the right way.

Call 416-907-0568Get My Fixed Quote

Let Us Prepare Your Real Estate Tax Return

Statement of Rental Income (T776)

We prepare your T776 to report rental income and expenses, such as mortgage interest, property tax, insurance, utilities, repairs, maintenance and management fees. We also review capital cost allowance (depreciation) and whether claiming it makes sense for you.

Capital Gains Schedules for Properties Sold

When you sell an investment property, we prepare the capital gains schedules and calculate the adjusted cost base, including eligible improvements and selling costs.

Property Flipping and Short-Term Sales

If you buy and sell real estate frequently, profits may be taxed as business income rather than capital gains. Residential property held for less than 12 months is generally treated as business income under the property flipping rules, with some life-event exceptions. We review your sales and report them correctly.

Principal Residence Sales

When you sell your home, the sale must still be reported, along with the principal residence designation. We make sure it is reported properly so you keep the exemption you are entitled to.

GST/HST New Residential Rental Property Rebate

If you bought a newly built home or condo to rent out, you may qualify for the GST/HST new residential rental property rebate. We help you check eligibility and file the application.

Rental, flip or home sale? One CPA team can handle all your property reporting.

Book a ConsultationCall 416-907-0568

Owning Property Personally or Through a Corporation

Some investors hold property in their own name, while others use a corporation. Each option has different tax rates, costs and filing requirements.

  • Owned personally: rental income and gains are reported on your personal tax return.
  • Owned through a corporation: income is reported on the corporate tax return, and the corporation needs year-end financial statements.

We explain the trade-offs for your situation and help you choose. If you plan to set up a holding company, our incorporation and business registration services can help.

From Filing to Planning

Let us take care of all your real estate matters, from filing taxes to preparing financial statements and planning ahead. Our real estate tax planning covers the timing of sales, ownership structure and how to reduce tax on future gains. Investors with many units can also keep their records current with our bookkeeping services.

Who We Help

  • Landlords with a basement unit, condo or house
  • Investors with several rental properties
  • Owners who sold an investment property or a home
  • People who buy, renovate and resell property
  • Corporations that own real estate
  • Non-residents who own property in Canada. See our non-resident tax return services.

Our Process

  1. Consultation. We learn about your properties, ownership and any sales.
  2. Fixed quote. You know the full cost before any work begins.
  3. Document collection. We send a checklist of statements, receipts and purchase or sale documents. See our tax checklists.
  4. Preparation and CPA review. We prepare your T776, capital gains schedules and returns.
  5. Filing. We file with CRA and give you a clear summary.
  6. Planning. We review what you can do differently next year to lower tax.

Thinking of buying or selling property? Talk to a CPA before you sign.

Contact Us TodayCall 416-907-0568

Repairs vs. Capital Improvements

One of the most common real estate tax questions is whether an expense can be deducted right away or must be added to the cost of the property. Day-to-day repairs that restore a property to its original condition, such as fixing a leaking tap or repainting, are usually deductible in the year they are paid. Improvements that make the property better than it was, such as a new roof with better materials, a renovated kitchen or an added unit, are usually capital costs.

Capital costs are claimed over time through capital cost allowance and also increase the property’s cost when it is sold, which can reduce the capital gain. Getting this classification right matters for both your yearly rental income and your tax when you sell. We review your expenses and record them correctly.

Serving Property Owners Across the GTA and Ontario

Our office is at 2 County Court Blvd, Suite 400, in Brampton. We serve real estate investors in Brampton, Mississauga, Caledon, Bolton, Georgetown, Milton, Toronto, Etobicoke, Vaughan, Oakville and across Ontario.

At Bajwa CPA, we take the time to learn about and understand each client’s business or situation to make sure we truly meet their needs and provide outstanding professional service. Our goal is to deliver our services in an easy-to-understand manner that is both timely and reliable.

Frequently Asked Questions

What expenses can I claim on a rental property?

Common expenses include mortgage interest, property tax, insurance, utilities you pay, repairs and maintenance, advertising and management fees. Larger improvements are usually capital costs claimed over time.

Do I have to report the sale of my home?

Yes. Even if the sale is fully exempt as your principal residence, it must be reported on your return.

Is profit from flipping a house a capital gain?

Usually not. Frequent buying and selling, and most sales of residential property owned for less than 12 months, are generally taxed as business income.

Should I hold my rental property in a corporation?

It depends on your income, the number of properties and your long-term plans. We compare personal and corporate ownership with your numbers.

Can I claim the GST/HST rebate on a new rental property?

You may qualify if you bought a newly built residential property and rent it out on a long-term basis. We check the rules for your property.

trust-estate-tax-return.content:
Losing a family member is hard enough without worrying about CRA filings. At Bajwa CPA Professional Corporation, we help executors, trustees and families in Brampton, Mississauga and across the Greater Toronto Area file trust and estate tax returns correctly and on time. A licensed CPA prepares and reviews every return, you get a fixed quote before work begins, and we stay with you until the estate is fully wound up.

Under Canadian tax law, a family trust is a personal trust and must follow the rules for personal trusts. There are two basic types of personal trusts:

  • Testamentary trust: a trust that comes into existence on the death of the person who made the will.
  • Inter vivos trust: a trust created while the person is alive, for the benefit of other living people.

Each type has its own filing rules, deadlines and planning opportunities. We explain them in plain language and handle the paperwork for you.

Why Executors Work With a CPA

An executor is personally responsible for making sure the deceased’s taxes are filed and paid before the estate’s assets are handed to the beneficiaries. If assets are distributed too early and CRA later finds tax owing, the executor can be held liable for it.

Estate filings often involve more than one return, deemed sales of investments and property at death, RRSP or RRIF balances, and deadlines that depend on the date of death. Getting this right protects the executor, reduces tax for the family and avoids delays in settling the estate.

Named as an executor? Let a CPA handle the CRA side so you can focus on your family.

Call 416-907-0568Get My Fixed Quote

Testamentary Trusts and Estate Returns

When a person passes away, the executor has to file a T1 tax return for the last year of the deceased’s life. Along with this final personal tax return, a trust tax return, or T3 return, may need to be filed for the estate. Our personal tax return services cover the final T1, so both returns are prepared together.

An estate or trust is treated as a “person” for tax purposes and has to file a return each year to report income. An estate’s tax year begins the day after the person passes away. Any income the estate earns, such as capital gains, dividends or interest, is reported on the T3 return and offset against available deductions.

If an estate carries on for several years, a T3 return has to be filed for each year. When the estate is wound up and all assets have been distributed, the executor should request a Tax Clearance Certificate from CRA to confirm that all taxes have been paid. We prepare and submit this request for you.

It is best to discuss with the experts at Bajwa CPA how to proceed with tax filings and other regulatory requirements for your estate.

Inter Vivos Trusts

An inter vivos trust is created while a person is alive, usually for family members. Income kept inside this kind of trust is taxed at the highest marginal tax rate. However, when an income-producing asset is held in the trust, its income and capital gains can often be flowed through to beneficiaries whose tax rates are lower.

Many tax planning techniques can be applied when preparing returns for these trusts. We prepare your trust returns and advise whether tax on income earned by an estate or trust can be shared among the beneficiaries rather than paid by the trust itself. For broader strategy, see our tax planning services.

Our Trust & Estate Tax Services

Final T1 Return for the Deceased

We report income up to the date of death, including deemed dispositions of investments and property, and RRSP or RRIF balances.

T3 Trust and Estate Returns

We prepare annual T3 returns for estates and trusts, including information returns where no income was earned.

Tax Clearance Certificates

We request the clearance certificate from CRA before final distribution, so the executor is protected.

Beneficiary Reporting

We prepare T3 slips so income allocated to beneficiaries is reported correctly on their own returns.

Trust Tax Planning

We look for ways to lower the overall tax paid by the trust and its beneficiaries.

Estate Property and Real Estate

Estates that hold rental or investment property often need extra schedules. Our real estate tax return services cover these properties. If a beneficiary or the deceased lived outside Canada, our non-resident tax return services can help.

Final T1, T3 returns and clearance certificate handled by one CPA team.

Book a ConsultationCall 416-907-0568

Our Process for Executors

  1. Consultation. We review the will, the date of death and the estate’s assets.
  2. Fixed quote. You know the full cost before any work begins.
  3. Document collection. We give you a simple list of slips, statements and records to gather. See our tax checklists.
  4. Final T1 and T3 preparation. A CPA prepares and reviews each return.
  5. Filing and CRA follow-up. We file the returns and respond to any CRA questions.
  6. Clearance certificate. We request it before you distribute the remaining assets.

Not sure which returns the estate needs? Ask a CPA before you distribute any assets.

Ask a CPACall 416-907-0568

Serving Executors Across the GTA and Ontario

Our office is at 2 County Court Blvd, Suite 400, in Brampton. We help executors and families in Brampton, Mississauga, Caledon, Bolton, Georgetown, Milton, Toronto, Etobicoke, Vaughan, Oakville and across Ontario.

Why Families Choose Bajwa CPA

At Bajwa CPA, we take the time to learn about and understand each client’s situation to make sure we truly meet their needs and provide outstanding professional service. Our goal is to deliver our services in an easy-to-understand manner that is both timely and reliable. We know estate matters are personal, so we explain every step clearly and with care.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the final tax return due after someone passes away?

It depends on the date of death. If the person died between January and October, the final return is generally due by April 30 of the following year. If they died in November or December, it is generally due six months after the date of death.

Does every estate need a T3 return?

Not always. A T3 return is needed when the estate earns income or has other filing requirements. Even when no income is earned, an information return may still be required. We confirm what applies.

What is a clearance certificate and why does it matter?

It is a certificate from CRA confirming that all taxes owed by the deceased or the estate have been paid. Getting it before distributing assets protects the executor from being personally liable for unpaid tax.

How is an inter vivos trust taxed?

Income kept in an inter vivos trust is taxed at the highest marginal rate. Income paid or allocated to beneficiaries is usually taxed in their hands instead, often at lower rates.

How much does an estate return cost?

It depends on the number of returns and the estate’s assets. You get a fixed quote after a consultation, before any work begins.

incorporation-business-registration.content:
Starting a business or ready to incorporate? Bajwa CPA Professional Corporation helps entrepreneurs and professionals in Brampton, Mississauga and across the Greater Toronto Area set up their business the right way from day one. We are very experienced in providing incorporation services, both federal and provincial, and business registration services for business corporations, professional corporations and not-for-profit corporations.

We also offer NUANS name searches, business name registration, and the registration of sole proprietorships and general partnerships. Your setup is handled by a licensed CPA, priced with a fixed quote, and backed by support all year as your business grows.

Why Set Up Your Business With a CPA?

The way you set up your business affects how much tax you pay, how you pay yourself and how much paperwork you face every year. Online incorporation services can file the forms, but they rarely tell you whether incorporating makes sense, which year end to choose or how to structure your shares.

Because we also prepare corporate tax returns, we set up your corporation with your future tax filings in mind. That means fewer surprises at your first year end and a structure that supports your goals.

Thinking about incorporating? Find out if it makes sense for your income before you file.

Call 416-907-0568Get My Fixed Quote

Federal vs. Ontario Incorporation

You can incorporate federally under the Canada Business Corporations Act or provincially under Ontario’s Business Corporations Act. A federal corporation can use its name across Canada, while an Ontario corporation is simpler when you plan to operate only in Ontario. We explain the differences, including name protection and filing requirements, and help you choose the option that fits your plans.

Who We Help Register

Business Corporations

For owners who want limited liability, lower corporate tax rates on retained profits and room to grow.

Professional Corporations

For doctors, dentists, chiropractors, pharmacists and other regulated professionals who are allowed to practise through a corporation.

Not-for-Profit Corporations

For community groups, associations and charities that need a formal legal structure.

Sole Proprietorships and General Partnerships

For new or smaller businesses that want a simple, low-cost start. When you are ready, we prepare your business tax return each year.

Our Business Registration Services Include

  • Conducting preliminary name searches and obtaining NUANS name search reports
  • Preparing Articles of Incorporation
  • Drafting share conditions, as appropriate
  • Preparing organizational board and shareholder resolutions and related corporate documents to issue shares
  • Electing directors and appointing officers
  • Enacting the general operating by-law and borrowing by-law
  • Selecting the financial year end
  • Completing minute book registers and ledgers, and assembling the minute book for delivery to you
  • Business name registration in Ontario

We can handle all of your incorporation and business registration needs anywhere in Ontario and Canada.

NUANS search, articles, by-laws and minute book, all done for you by one CPA team.

Book a ConsultationCall 416-907-0568

Should You Incorporate?

Incorporating is not right for every business. A corporation can offer lower tax on profits you leave in the business, limited liability and more flexibility in how you pay yourself. It also comes with extra costs, including annual corporate tax returns, financial statements and more bookkeeping.

We review your income, expenses and plans, then show you the numbers side by side. If it makes sense to stay a sole proprietor for now, we tell you. For a deeper review, see our tax planning services or our business consulting services.

After You Incorporate

Setting up the corporation is only the first step. We can also help with:

  • Bookkeeping and accounting setup so your records are ready for year end. See our bookkeeping services.
  • Year-end financial statements for your corporation, lenders and CRA. Learn about our financial statement services.
  • Corporate tax returns (T2), payroll, and T4 and T5 slips for owners and employees.
  • Salary vs. dividends advice so you pay yourself in the most tax-efficient way.

Our Simple Process

  1. Consultation. We discuss your business, goals and whether incorporating is the right move.
  2. Fixed quote. You know the full cost before any work begins.
  3. Name search. We run a preliminary search and obtain a NUANS report.
  4. Incorporation documents. We prepare articles, share conditions, by-laws and resolutions.
  5. Filing. We file with the federal or Ontario government.
  6. Minute book delivery. You receive a completed minute book, ready for your records.

Start your corporation on the right foot. Speak with a Brampton CPA today.

Contact Us TodayCall 416-907-0568

Common Incorporation Mistakes We Help You Avoid

Many new owners incorporate quickly online and only find problems at their first year end. Common issues include choosing a year end that does not suit the business, issuing shares without proper resolutions, keeping no minute book, and mixing personal and corporate bank accounts. Others forget that a corporation must file its own T2 return every year, even with no income, and may need to register for HST and payroll accounts with CRA.

When we set up your corporation, we look ahead to these issues. We help you choose a sensible year end, put the right share structure in place from the start and prepare complete corporate records. We also explain the ongoing filings your new corporation will have, so you start your first year with clear expectations and no surprises.

Serving New Businesses Across the GTA and Ontario

Our office is at 2 County Court Blvd, Suite 400, in Brampton. We incorporate and register businesses for entrepreneurs in Brampton, Mississauga, Caledon, Bolton, Georgetown, Milton, Toronto, Etobicoke, Vaughan, Oakville and across Ontario.

At Bajwa CPA, we take the time to learn about and understand each client’s business to make sure we truly meet their needs and provide outstanding professional service. Our goal is to deliver our services in an easy-to-understand manner that is both timely and reliable.

Should I incorporate federally or in Ontario?

If you plan to operate only in Ontario, a provincial corporation is often simpler. If you want name protection across Canada or plan to expand to other provinces, a federal corporation may be the better choice.

What is a NUANS report?

A NUANS report is a name search that compares your proposed corporate name with existing business names and trademarks. It is generally required when incorporating with a name rather than a number.

Can a professional incorporate?

Many regulated professionals, such as doctors, dentists, chiropractors and pharmacists, can practise through a professional corporation, subject to the rules of their governing body.

Do I need to register a sole proprietorship in Ontario?

If you operate under a business name that is different from your own legal name, you generally need to register that name in Ontario.

What is a minute book?

A minute book holds your corporation’s key records, including articles, by-laws, resolutions and registers of directors, officers and shareholders. We prepare and deliver it to you.

financial-statements.title: Financial Statements
financial-statements.content:
Accurate financial statements are vital for corporations and businesses, because many people rely on them. Banks, lenders, investors, and the federal and provincial governments all use the financial information prepared for your business. At Bajwa CPA Professional Corporation, we prepare clear, accurate year-end financial statements for businesses in Brampton, Mississauga and across the Greater Toronto Area.

Every set of statements is prepared and reviewed by a licensed CPA, priced with a fixed quote, and supported all year so you understand what your numbers mean.

Why Accurate Financial Statements Matter

It is extremely important that financial statements are prepared following sound accounting principles. Well-prepared statements help you:

  • File accurate corporate tax returns and business tax returns
  • Meet bank or lender restrictive covenants
  • Apply for external financing
  • Prepare government filings, such as payroll, on time
  • Prepare HST and tax returns
  • Build budgets, forecasts and projections for your company

Our tax and accounting firm makes sure your financial statements are accurate and classified in line with Canadian accounting standards.

Need statements for your bank, lender or year end? Get them prepared by a CPA.

Call 416-907-0568Get My Fixed Quote

Preparation of Annual Financial Statements

Your annual financial statements show the full picture of your business for the year. We prepare:

Balance Sheet

What your business owns, what it owes and the owner’s equity at year end.

Income Statement

Your revenue, expenses and profit for the year, so you can see how the business performed.

Notes and Supporting Schedules

Additional details your bank, lender or CRA may need to understand the numbers.

We use your books and records to prepare these statements. If your records need work first, our bookkeeping services can get them up to date.

Compilation Engagements (Notice to Reader)

In a compilation engagement, the financial statements are compiled from information provided by management or the owner. In this report, we act as accountants and not as auditors. There is no attempt to audit, review or verify the accuracy or completeness of the information, and the report says so clearly.

Compilation engagements were long known as “Notice to Reader” (NTR) engagements. Under current Canadian standards, they are issued with a compilation engagement report. Either way, they are the most common type of year-end statements for small and medium-sized private businesses in Ontario, and they are widely accepted by banks and lenders for financing.

Applying for a loan or line of credit? We prepare compiled statements your lender can use.

Book a ConsultationCall 416-907-0568

Who Needs Financial Statements?

  • Corporations filing a T2 return, which requires financial information with every return.
  • Business owners applying for financing, such as loans, mortgages or lines of credit.
  • Companies with lender covenants that must provide statements every year.
  • Real estate investors holding properties personally or through a corporation. See our real estate tax return services.
  • Owners planning to grow, sell or bring in partners, who need reliable numbers for decisions.

How Financial Statements Support Planning

Good financial statements are not just for CRA. They give you a starting point for budgeting and forecasting, help you spot trends in costs and margins, and support smarter tax planning before your next year end. If you are planning to buy, sell or restructure, our business consulting services build on these numbers.

Our Process

  1. Consultation. We learn about your business, year end and who will use the statements.
  2. Fixed quote. You know the full cost before any work begins.
  3. Records review. We review your books, bank statements and supporting documents.
  4. Adjustments. We propose year-end adjusting entries where needed.
  5. Preparation and CPA review. We prepare the statements and the compilation engagement report.
  6. Delivery and explanation. We walk you through the results and how they affect your tax return.

Year end coming up? Book early and get your statements on time.

Contact Us TodayCall 416-907-0568

What We Need From You

Preparing financial statements is faster and less costly when your records are organized. Most businesses will need to provide:

  • Bank and credit card statements for the full year
  • Your bookkeeping file or general ledger, if you keep one
  • Sales and purchase invoices, or summaries of them
  • Loan, lease and line of credit statements
  • Payroll summaries and HST returns filed during the year
  • Details of any equipment, vehicles or property bought or sold
  • Last year’s financial statements and tax return

If some of these are missing, we will tell you exactly what is needed and help you fill the gaps. A clear checklist means fewer back-and-forth questions and statements delivered on time for your lender or your tax filing deadline.

Serving Businesses Across the GTA and Ontario

Our office is at 2 County Court Blvd, Suite 400, in Brampton. We prepare financial statements for businesses in Brampton, Mississauga, Caledon, Bolton, Georgetown, Milton, Toronto, Etobicoke, Vaughan, Oakville and across Ontario.

Why Choose Bajwa CPA

At Bajwa CPA, we take the time to learn about and understand each client’s business to make sure we truly meet their needs and provide outstanding professional service. Our goal is to deliver our services in an easy-to-understand manner that is both timely and reliable. We work with consultants, medical and dental professionals, construction companies, retail stores, automotive businesses, real estate brokerages, franchises and many more.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between a compilation, a review and an audit?

A compilation puts your financial information into statement form without verifying it. A review provides limited assurance through inquiry and analysis. An audit provides the highest level of assurance. Most small private businesses only need a compilation.

Is a Notice to Reader the same as a compilation engagement?

Yes. “Notice to Reader” was the older name. Compilation engagements are now issued under updated Canadian standards with a compilation engagement report.

Will my bank accept compiled financial statements?

Most banks and lenders accept compiled statements for small and medium-sized businesses. Some larger loans may require a review or audit, so check with your lender.

Do I need financial statements to file my corporate tax return?

Yes. Corporations must include financial information with their T2 return, so year-end statements are part of the process.

How much do financial statements cost?

It depends on the size of your business and the condition of your records. You get a fixed quote after a consultation.

Get Your Financial Statements Prepared

Looking for a CPA to prepare financial statements in Brampton or Mississauga? Call 416-907-0568 or contact us today to book a consultation.

tax-planning.title: Tax Planning
tax-planning.content:
At Bajwa CPA, we understand the complexities of the Canadian tax system. Our experienced team develops customized tax planning strategies, both corporate and personal, that support your company’s future success, improve your cash flow and increase your personal wealth. We help individuals, business owners and investors in Brampton, Mississauga and across the Greater Toronto Area pay the lowest tax the law allows.

Tax planning is a legal way to reduce tax. We guide you through the tax laws and recommend deductions and strategies that help you keep more of what you earn. You work one-on-one with a licensed CPA, receive a fixed quote before work begins, and get support all year, not just at filing time.

Why Plan Ahead Instead of Waiting for Tax Season?

Tax planning should be done at the beginning of the fiscal year, not when you file your annual return. By the time your return is being prepared, most opportunities to lower tax for that year have already passed.

Planning early lets you time income and expenses, choose how to pay yourself from your corporation, make the most of registered accounts and avoid surprises at year end. The result is lower tax, steadier cash flow and fewer last-minute decisions.

The best time to cut next year’s tax bill is now. Talk to a CPA before your year end.

Call 416-907-0568Book a Planning Session

Our Tax Planning Services

Corporate Tax Planning

We help incorporated businesses lower tax and plan cash flow. This includes salary vs. dividends advice for shareholders, advice on shareholder loans and advances, timing of large purchases and year-end planning. We then carry these plans into your corporate tax return.

Personal Tax Planning

We help individuals and families make full use of personal tax deductions and credits, RRSP, TFSA and FHSA contributions, and income splitting where allowed. Your plan is reflected in your personal tax return each year.

Real Estate Tax Planning

Whether you own rental property or buy and sell real estate, how you hold and report it affects your tax. We review whether to own property personally or through a corporation and how sales will be taxed. Learn more on our real estate tax return page.

Non-Resident Tax Planning

If you are leaving Canada, living abroad or earning Canadian income as a non-resident, we plan for departure tax, withholding tax and treaty relief. See our non-resident tax return services.

Investment Portfolio Review

We review your capital gains and losses to see where tax can be reduced, such as using losses to offset gains.

Preparation of Tax Opinions

We prepare written tax opinions on specific transactions or questions, so you understand the tax effect before you act.

Salary or dividends? Corporation or personal? Get a clear answer from a CPA.

Ask a CPACall 416-907-0568

Examples of Tax Planning Strategies

Every plan is built around your situation, but common strategies include:

  • Using personal tax deductions and credits that are often missed, such as medical, childcare, tuition and donation credits.
  • Reviewing investments for capital gains and losses to manage tax on sales.
  • Salary vs. dividends advice for corporate shareholders, balancing tax today with RRSP room and CPP.
  • Shareholder loan and advance planning to avoid unexpected tax on money taken from a corporation.
  • Registered account strategy using RRSPs, TFSAs and FHSAs.
  • Choosing the right business structure, such as staying a sole proprietor or incorporating. Our incorporation and business registration services can help when the time is right.

Who We Help

  • Business owners and incorporated professionals who want to pay themselves efficiently.
  • Self-employed individuals deciding when to incorporate. See our business tax return page.
  • Families looking to reduce household tax.
  • Real estate investors with one or more properties.
  • Non-residents and people leaving Canada.
  • Executors and trustees managing estates and trusts. Visit our trust and estate tax return services.

Our Tax Planning Process

  1. Consultation. We learn about your income, business, investments and goals.
  2. Fixed quote. You know the cost before any work begins.
  3. Review. We review past returns, financial statements and current plans.
  4. Recommendations. We present clear options and the tax savings for each.
  5. Action. We help you put the plan in place before your year end.
  6. Year-round follow-up. We revisit the plan as your situation or the tax rules change.

Take advantage of these strategies today. Book your tax planning consultation.

Contact Us TodayCall 416-907-0568

Common Tax Planning Mistakes We See

Many people only think about tax when they file, which means they miss savings every year. Common mistakes include taking money out of a corporation without a plan, which can create unexpected tax on shareholder loans; contributing to registered accounts without considering which one fits best; selling investments without reviewing available capital losses; and buying or selling property without first checking how the sale will be taxed.

Business owners also often pay themselves the same way year after year, even when their income or goals have changed. A short planning review each year can catch these issues early. We look at your whole picture, both personal and business, so each decision supports the others and you keep more of what you earn.

Serving Clients Across the GTA and Ontario

Our office is at 2 County Court Blvd, Suite 400, in Brampton. We provide tax planning to individuals and businesses in Brampton, Mississauga, Caledon, Bolton, Georgetown, Milton, Toronto, Etobicoke, Vaughan, Oakville and across Ontario.

At Bajwa CPA, we take the time to learn about and understand each client’s business or situation to make sure we truly meet their needs and provide outstanding professional service. Our goal is to deliver our services in an easy-to-understand manner that is both timely and reliable.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is tax planning legal?

Yes. Tax planning uses the rules in the tax law, such as deductions, credits and the choice of business structure, to legally reduce the tax you pay.

When should I start tax planning?

Ideally at the start of your fiscal year. Many strategies must be in place before year end to have an effect.

Should I pay myself a salary or dividends from my corporation?

It depends on your income needs, RRSP and CPP goals, and your corporation’s profits. We compare both options with your actual numbers.

Can tax planning help if I only have employment income?

Yes. Employees can still benefit from RRSP, TFSA and FHSA strategy, credits and deductions, and planning for investments or rental income.

How much does tax planning cost?

It depends on how complex your situation is. You get a fixed quote after a consultation, before any work begins.

Start Planning Today

Looking for tax planning services in Brampton or Mississauga? Call 416-907-0568 or contact us today to book an appointment and discuss your accounting and tax needs.

budgeting-forecasting.title: Budgeting & Forecasting
budgeting-forecasting.content:
Budgeting is an important part of financial success for any business. A budget is your business’s financial plan to better manage monthly, quarterly and annual cash coming in and going out. Forecasting uses your historical data to make financial projections for the longer term.

At Bajwa CPA Professional Corporation, we help small and medium-sized businesses in Brampton, Mississauga, Toronto and across the Greater Toronto Area build budgets and forecasts they can actually use. Our accountants are well experienced in providing high-quality, efficient budgeting services at very competitive rates. Your plan is built with a licensed CPA, priced with a fixed quote and supported all year.

Why Budgeting and Forecasting Matter

Many businesses only look at their numbers once a year, when the tax return is due. By then, it is too late to fix a cash shortfall or take advantage of an opportunity. A clear budget and forecast let you see problems and opportunities months ahead, so you can act early instead of reacting.

Whether you are planning to hire, expand, buy equipment, apply for financing or simply get through a slow season, a budget and forecast give you the numbers to decide with confidence.

Tired of guessing where your cash will be next quarter? Let a CPA build your plan.

Call 416-907-0568Get My Fixed Quote

Budgeting With Our Tax Experts

A well-built budget:

  • Provides a benchmark for measuring performance against your financial goals and objectives
  • Helps you allocate financial resources between different parts of your business
  • Works as a communication tool to share your financial goals with partners, managers and lenders
  • Lets you authorize the use of financial resources with clear limits and priorities

We build your budget from your actual financial statements and bookkeeping records, so it reflects how your business really runs. If your records need to be updated first, our bookkeeping services can help.

Forecasting With Our Advisors

A good forecast:

  • Gives you information to make smart business decisions
  • Helps you spot unexpected issues early, so you can take corrective action in time
  • Lets you identify potential opportunities quickly
  • Communicates expected financial results to owners, investors and lenders

Planning to hire, expand or borrow? See the numbers before you commit.

Book a ConsultationCall 416-907-0568

What We Can Prepare for You

Annual Operating Budgets

A month-by-month plan for revenue, expenses and profit for the coming year.

Cash Flow Forecasts

A view of when money will come in and go out, so you can plan for slow months, tax payments and HST remittances.

Financial Projections

Longer-term projections built from your historical results, useful for growth plans and lender applications.

Budget vs. Actual Reviews

A comparison of your actual results against the budget, so you can see what is on track and what needs attention.

How Budgeting Connects to Your Taxes

Budgets and forecasts are not separate from your tax and accounting work. They rely on accurate financial statements, and they make tax planning far more effective. When you know your expected profit, you can plan instalments, decide how to pay yourself and time large purchases before year end. Incorporated businesses can carry this planning into their corporate tax return.

If you need broader advice on pricing, structure or financing, our business consulting services build on your budget and forecast.

Who We Help

  • Startups preparing their first year of operations
  • Growing businesses planning to hire or expand
  • Owners applying for loans or lines of credit
  • Franchises and multi-location operators
  • Construction, retail, automotive, food and professional service businesses

Our Process

  1. Consultation. We learn about your business, goals and current numbers.
  2. Fixed quote. You know the full cost before any work begins.
  3. Data review. We review your financial statements and bookkeeping records.
  4. Build the plan. We prepare your budget, forecast or projections.
  5. Walkthrough. We explain the results and the key numbers to watch.
  6. Ongoing review. We update the plan and compare results through the year.

Get a budget and forecast that helps you grow. Start with a conversation.

Contact Us TodayCall 416-907-0568

What You Need to Get Started

Building a useful budget or forecast starts with good information. We usually ask for your last one or two years of financial statements, your current bookkeeping file, a list of fixed monthly costs such as rent, loans and payroll, and any known plans for the year ahead, such as new hires, equipment purchases or price changes.

If your books are behind, we can bring them up to date first so the plan is based on accurate numbers. Once the budget is in place, we suggest a simple monthly or quarterly check-in to compare actual results and adjust the forecast. This keeps the plan useful all year, rather than a document that is filed away and forgotten.

Serving Businesses Across the GTA and Ontario

Our office is at 2 County Court Blvd, Suite 400, in Brampton. We provide budgeting and forecasting for businesses in Brampton, Mississauga, Toronto, Caledon, Bolton, Georgetown, Milton, Etobicoke, Vaughan, Oakville and across Ontario.

At Bajwa CPA, we take the time to learn about and understand each client’s business to make sure we truly meet their needs and provide outstanding professional service. Our goal is to deliver our services in an easy-to-understand manner that is both timely and reliable.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between a budget and a forecast?

A budget is your plan for what you want to happen, usually for the next year. A forecast estimates what is likely to happen, based on your historical results and current trends.

How often should a budget be reviewed?

Most businesses benefit from comparing actual results to the budget monthly or quarterly, and updating the forecast as conditions change.

Do I need a budget to apply for a business loan?

Many lenders ask for projections or cash flow forecasts along with your financial statements, especially for new businesses or larger loans.

Can a small business benefit from budgeting?

Yes. Even a simple budget helps a small business manage cash, plan for tax payments and avoid surprises.

How much does budgeting and forecasting cost?

It depends on the size of your business and what you need prepared. You get a fixed quote after a consultation.

Plan Your Next Move With Confidence

Looking for budgeting and forecasting services in Brampton or Mississauga? Call 416-907-0568 or contact us today to book a consultation.
